Definition: from θρέομαι to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten:--trouble.
BiblicalUsage: throéō stands behind the English phrase to be troubled, to be frightened. In Matthew 24:6, see that ye be not troubled, and it appears again in 2 Thessalonians 2:2. In the Greek text the word is spelled θροέομαι.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that I need not be troubled by what is coming, because the God who told me in advance is the God who holds me.
